title: The Seven Grades from the Itinerarium

blocks.s: In the book called The Journey of the Mind to God (Itinerarius mentis in Deum), Bonaventure assigns grades or species of contemplation by which the soul ascends, as by successive steps, to the speculation of the eternal Divinity and the most blessed Trinity. The first grade is the contemplation of God through his vestiges in the universe; the second is the contemplation of God through his vestiges in this sensible world — both of which were already discussed in Book One, in those articles concerning the fifth species of contemplation (articles sixty-eight and sixty-nine). The third is the contemplation of God through his image naturally impressed in the soul, namely the rational soul — of which also something was said in Book One, articles seventy and seventy-one. The fourth is the contemplation of God through his image reformed by gratuitous gifts — treated in Book One in those articles concerning the fourth species of contemplation. The fifth is the contemplation of the divine unity through its primary name, which is Being — treated in article twelve of Book One. The sixth is the contemplation of the most blessed Trinity through its name which is Good — treated in Book One in those articles concerning the first species of contemplation. The seventh is mental and mystical excess, in which rest is given to the intellect, the affection wholly passing over into God — which must be treated more carefully, God granting, in Book Three below.
